A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OmniFC, with matching core algorithms, theorems, experiments and appendices. Their text, equations, tables and figures are readable and support a reliable comparison, including v2's additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original clustering experiments on seven datasets, Kappa and NMI results, distance-reconstruction comparisons and hyperparameter/sample-size sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds reconstruction timings, Dirichlet-partition experiments and results for a deep-clustering extension.

M1.justification: Appendix D.4 adds OmniFC-DCN, which supplies reconstructed distances as features to the deep clustering method DCN. This introduces a deep-clustering backend while retaining the existing encoding, distance reconstruction and clustering variants.

E1.justification: The same seven datasets and clustering tasks are retained. Dirichlet partitions of Pendigits, larger subsets of 10x_73k and DCN experiments on existing datasets change partitioning, sample sizes or model configuration rather than dataset/task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 10 adds an internal comparison of OmniFC-DCN against OmniFC-KM. The original external and centralized comparator sets remain unchanged and are reused in the Dirichlet experiment. SecFC and newly cited secure-clustering methods are not newly benchmarked.

E3.justification: New experiments use Dirichlet concentrations 1000, 5 and 0.001 on Pendigits, and measure reconstruction time on 1,000–70,000 samples from 10x_73k with l = 2, 4 and 8. Existing benchmark metrics, partition protocol, default hyperparameters and subsampling policy are retained; these additions do not establish reruns of the original experiments.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's reconstruction-fidelity and hyperparameter/sample-size checks, v2 adds computational scalability analysis across sample counts and segmentation choices, robustness under Dirichlet label heterogeneity, and a deep-versus-shallow feasibility study. Section 3.4 and Appendices D.3–D.4 substantially broaden the practical questions investigated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. v2's checklist explicitly acknowledges the absence of statistical-significance reporting and invokes deterministic reconstruction, but does not document a new repeated-run or uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: The original Kappa, NMI and sample-size RMSE values are unchanged. New Table 4 reports 70,000-sample reconstruction times of 13,576 seconds at l = 2 and 4,352 at l = 8. Table 9 adds Dirichlet-setting results, while Table 10 reports OmniFC-DCN Kappa of 0.43/0.64/0.60 versus OmniFC-KM's 0.42/0.62/0.56 on MNIST/Pendigits/10x_73k. These are additional experiments, not version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: New Section 3.4 supplies asymptotic computational bounds for client encoding/distance computation and server decoding. The two main theorems, reconstruction/privacy condition and appendix proofs remain substantively unchanged. The explicit interpolation formula newly displayed in Equation (5) expands an already defined construction.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: model-agnostic federated clustering through secure, lossless distance reconstruction, resistance to heterogeneity and empirical effectiveness. The supplementary additions support these claims without materially redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 explains the opposing client/server computational effects of segmentation and the efficiency-versus-collusion-protection tradeoff between l and t. It interprets the new timings as evidence of practical scalability and the DCN experiment as initial deep-clustering feasibility. The limitation concerning shallow methods and complex/high-dimensional data remains.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit server interpolation formula, reconstruction timings and guidance on choosing l and t under the recovery constraint. Hardware, software-library disclosures, default values and subsampling instructions are retained. Code remains promised, with the new checklist specifying release upon publication; detailed DCN training settings are not supplied.

R1.justification: Section 2 newly identifies SecFC as the closest work and distinguishes OmniFC through broader clustering compatibility and one-shot communication. Eleven references are added, covering secure clustering, privacy, computational tools and deep/federated clustering; the earlier cited works are retained. The overall research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 makes targeted explanatory additions, adds a complexity subsection and two supplementary experiment subsections, and includes acknowledgements and a NeurIPS checklist. Author/contact and venue text also change. Most existing scientific prose and the main narrative structure are retained rather than extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v2 adds three tables for timings, Dirichlet experiments and DCN results, enlarges Figure 1 vertically, and rearranges appendix tables and surrounding material. The original six figures retain their graphical content, and existing result tables retain their basic designs despite relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked runtime evidence and treated deep clustering as future work. v2 makes practical feasibility easier to assess through complexity bounds, measured reconstruction costs, alternative heterogeneity partitions and an initial deep-clustering demonstration, while clarifying its relationship to SecFC. These are useful gains, but sparse DCN training details, absent uncertainty estimates and code remaining only promised limit the overall improvement.
